jamal: Heads-up — brought up q8_2-long on the staging cluster, running the long-context prefill suite. seeing deterministic divergence vs fp16 after ~10k tokens. anyone seen this pattern before?

maya: ugh. which test? kv-prefill with causal priming or the streaming append suite?

jamal: kv-prefill + causal priming. test id `prefill-long-2026-03-20-01`. short repro attached below.

alex: can you paste the failing log snippet? also model build hash?

jamal: model: q8_2-long v0.9.3-rc2, build 20260319. log:```
[2026-03-20T01:05:12Z] run=pg1-prefill token=10241 mismatch_score=0.18
[2026-03-20T01:05:12Z] reference_checksum=0x7f3b9a5e
[2026-03-20T01:05:12Z] q8_check=0x6f3b8d4a
[2026-03-20T01:05:12Z] kv_prefill_window=16384 prefix_len=12000
```

maya: mismatch_score 0.18 is small but visible. do we get drift only at specific rotary phase boundaries?

jamal: looks like drift spikes when token index crosses a multiple of 4096. tried disabling rotary-rescale patch, no change.

eva: could be a quantized matmul ALU path that uses fused sparse kernels? any sparsity settings enabled in the quant profile?

jamal: quant profile: `entropy_aware: true`, `sparsity_threshold: 0.02`, `per_channel_scale: true`, `chunk_size: 128`. I ran a compare with entropy_aware=false and drift reduced but not eliminated.

li: did you try forcing plain GEMM (no kernel fusion) to see if it's a kernel bug vs quant scaling? small perf hit but useful for repro.

jamal: ran with `--runtime-force-gemm=true` on node set b3; logs show mismatch_score down to 0.02 but still non-zero at token 12160.

alex: interesting. that points to cumulative KV offset rather than single-op nondeterminism. do we have a kv write/evict off-by-one in tiled caches? show the prefill loop snippet.

jamal: snippet:```python
# prefill loop (pseudo)
for chunk in chunks(prompt, chunk_size=512):
    out = model.forward(chunk, use_kv_prefill=True)
    kv_store.append(out.kv)  # expects append at shard-aligned offsets
```

maya: if append assumes exact alignment but quant chunking changed internal tile size, you can get small misaligned writes that later shift indices. check `kv_store.offset_for_shard(shard_id)` and compare between q8 and fp16.

jamal: good call — offsets differ by 16 bytes sometimes on q8. traced to `serialize_kv_chunk` where `pad_to_chunk_boundary` uses `chunk_size_bytes = elems_per_chunk * 1` (should be *bytes_per_elem). PR incoming.

ci-bot: Pipeline prefill-long-2026-03-20-01 started on staging, job 6782.

eva: nice catch. curious if the pad bug only surfaces with entropy_aware quant because scale metadata changed element width assumptions.

jamal: repro plan: 1) land padding fix in staging, 2) re-run q8_2-long full prefill, 3) run slow gemm path to confirm kernel independence, 4) run A/B eval on 50 gold long-context prompts.

alex: also add a delta eval against rolling window checksums so we can pinpoint first divergence token. add `--emit-kv-checksums` to run.

maya: I'll own the A/B eval and goldset. jamal, ping me when the fix lands and you kick the job.

jamal: will do. one more note: logging shows occasional `kv_write_retry` on some shards — might be unrelated but adding to the checklist.

li: if we hit `kv_write_retry` we should surface it in the console as a per-route metric; filed ENG-PLAT-984 for follow-up.

jamal: thanks team. I'll open a short PR with the pad fix + unit test that compares offsets across quant modes.

eva: :thumbsup: and please include the failing prompt id in the ticket so we can regression-test on rollout.

jamal: added prompt ids to the ticket and CI repro. ci-bot will run prefill-long-2026-03-20-01 after merge.

ci-bot: Job 6782 queued; will run on merge to main.

alex: great thread. low-sev for now but important for long-tail correctness. keep us posted.
